packages.name: blyxtorch
packages.title: BlyxTorch
packages.description: Train dense networks with SGD or Adam, inspect parameter gradients, and generate standalone Blyx models for regression or classification.
packages.contract: BlyxTorch 0.2.0 uses fixed-shape float64 networks on CPU. Each layer width is 1–64. A model supports up to eight affine layers and 1,024 trainable parameters. The prebuilt 2–4–1 classifier runs immediately. Generating a new executable requires Blyx 0.2.1, Rust and a host linker on the build machine.
api: bt_dual(value, tangent), bt_square(v)
Differentiate a scalar expression in the portable library. The result holds its value and directional derivative.
bt_add, bt_sub, bt_mul, bt_div, bt_relu, bt_tanh, bt_sigmoid
Compose differentiable operations on dual numbers.
bt_init(seed), bt_predict(weights, features)
Initialize and run a generated model module.
bt_sample_loss(weights, features, target), bt_loss_grad(weights, features, target)
Return a loss or a loss followed by every parameter gradient.
blyxtorch emit WIDTHS OBJECTIVE ACTIVATION
Generate a complete Blyx model and CLI. Use mse, binary or softmax with tanh, relu or sigmoid.
train-score TRAIN.csv LABELLED.csv
Train once and report row count and loss on a separate labelled CSV.
train-predict TRAIN.csv FEATURES.csv
Train once and write a probability for each new feature row.
cli: Training writes a checkpoint to standard output. The handbook shows how to save it, predict and inspect gradients on each platform.

projects.title: Calibrate a desk sensor
projects.description: Fit a gain and an offset from five synthetic reference readings using BlyxTorch automatic differentiation. The model predicts 18.625 and 22.375 degrees for two readings held out of training.

projects.title: Predict print-queue waits
projects.description: Classify four new print jobs using a trained two-input network. The starter includes 16 synthetic training rows and six separate evaluation rows. With seed 7, the mean evaluation loss is about 0.00234.

packages.title: LinearFit
packages.description: Train, merge and deploy a single-feature least-squares or ridge regression with an unpenalized intercept.
packages.contract: Provide aligned finite x and y values. At least two rows are required. Set ridge to zero for ordinary least squares, or choose a positive penalty for shrinkage. The centered model keeps predictions stable for features with large offsets.
api: lf_fit(xs, ys, penalty)
Train on a pair of vectors. Returns [mean_x, mean_y, slope].
lf_start(), lf_update(state, x, y), lf_merge(a, b)
Accumulate rows or merge disjoint training batches.
lf_finish(state, penalty), lf_predict(model, x)
Freeze a model and predict a response in the original units.
lf_csv_summary(path)
Import the native csvfit module to read a CSV into a summary that lf_merge or lf_finish can use.
cli: The model learns slope 2 and predicts 11. Add --ridge 5 to shrink the slope to 1.
packages.logoAlt: Blyx penguin drawing a fitted line through scattered observations.

packages.title: Conformal
packages.description: Calibrate a regression interval from held-out errors and measure coverage on a separate test set.
packages.contract: Use examples held out from model training. Each interval is prediction ± a finite calibration radius. Coverage is marginal under exchangeability, and can differ by subgroup or after a distribution shift. A 90% request needs at least nine calibration examples for a finite interval.
api: cf_calibrate(actual, predicted, numerator, denominator)
Select an observed absolute residual using the finite-sample adjusted rank.
cf_radius(scores, numerator, denominator)
Calibrate from previously calculated nonnegative scores.
cf_interval(prediction, radius), cf_coverage(actual, predicted, radius)
Return the two endpoints, or measure the fraction of a separate test set covered.
packages.logoAlt: Blyx penguin holding an interval around a central point estimate.

packages.title: Moments
packages.description: Summarize paired observations as they arrive and merge statistics from independent batches.
packages.contract: The state contains count, two means, two centered sums of squares and a cross-product. Merge disjoint batches only. Empty batches act as the identity. Sample standard deviation needs at least two observations.
api: mom_empty(), mom_update(state, x, y)
Create a state and add one observation.
mom_summary(xs, ys), mom_merge(left, right)
Summarize vectors or combine batches in constant additional state.
mom_sample_sd_y(state)
Read the sample standard deviation of the second variable.
packages.logoAlt: Blyx penguin merging two groups of observations into one mean.

packages.title: ResidualWatch
packages.description: Monitor prediction drift by detecting sustained upward or downward changes in errors against a frozen reference period.
packages.contract: Keep rows in time order. The reference residual is actual minus prediction, so a positive alarm means sustained underprediction. A constant reference requires an explicit positive scale floor. Choose thresholds against representative stable data.
api: rw_fit(actual, predicted, min_scale)
Freeze row count, mean residual and sample scale from reference data.
rw_training(), rw_train(state, actual, prediction), rw_freeze(state, min_scale)
Learn the same reference one observation at a time.
rw_monitor(), rw_step(state, reference, actual, prediction, allowance, limit)
Update the detector. The third result is +1, −1 or 0.
cli: Reference residuals have mean 0 and sample deviation 1. The first alert is data row 5. The command exits with code 1.
packages.logoAlt: Blyx penguin watching residuals rise above a baseline on a monitor.

packages.title: CUSUM
packages.description: Detect persistent shifts in a sequence of standardized observations with a two-sided cumulative sum.
packages.contract: Supply standardized observations in order. The allowance controls how much deviation is ignored. The limit is inclusive. An observation following an alarm starts a fresh episode. Tune both values for the time series you monitor.
api: cs_empty()
Start with zero evidence of an upward or downward shift.
cs_step(state, z, allowance, limit)
Return [upward magnitude, downward magnitude, direction]. Save this state for the next point.
packages.logoAlt: Blyx penguin tracing cumulative steps across a threshold.

packages.title: ModelGate
packages.description: Compare two binary classifiers on the same observations and stop a release when mistake costs or Brier score regress.
packages.contract: Use paired labels and probabilities in [0,1]. A missed positive can carry a different cost from a false alarm. The sample has two models at 75% accuracy. With a miss costing five times as much, cost per prediction rises from 0.25 to 1.25.
api: gate_passes(baseline_brier, candidate_brier, baseline_cost, candidate_cost, tolerance)
Apply the gate to validated per-row metrics.
--threshold, --fn-cost, --fp-cost, --brier-tolerance
Configure costs and the maximum increase in mean Brier score.
cli: Returns exit code 1. Both models get three rows right, but the candidate misses the more costly positive.
packages.logoAlt: Blyx penguin at a model release gate with pass and stop signals.

packages.title: Classification
packages.description: Measure threshold decisions, false alarms, missed positives and their costs.
packages.contract: Inputs are equal-length vectors of binary labels and finite probabilities. A score equal to the threshold counts as positive. An undefined precision, recall or F1 has value zero.
api: class_confusion(labels, scores, threshold)
Return true positives, false positives, true negatives and false negatives in that order.
class_precision, class_recall, class_f1
Calculate scalar metrics from the confusion counts.
class_cost(fp, missed, fp_cost, fn_cost)
Compute total weighted cost. Divide by observation count for cost per row.
packages.logoAlt: Blyx penguin sorting circles and diamonds into a confusion matrix.

packages.title: Calibration
packages.description: Check agreement between predicted probabilities and observed outcomes.
packages.contract: Use equal-length, nonempty vectors of 0/1 labels and probabilities. Supply between one and 100 bins. A probability of 1 belongs in the last bin. The bin count matters when comparing expected calibration error.
api: cal_brier(labels, scores)
Compute mean squared probability error.
cal_bin(labels, scores, index, bins)
Return a reliability bin’s count, forecast total and outcome total.
cal_ece(labels, scores, bins)
Summarize bin gaps weighted by observation count.
packages.logoAlt: Blyx penguin comparing a calibration curve with a diagonal reference.

packages.title: Retrieval
packages.description: Score ranked search or RAG results without giving repeated document IDs extra credit.
packages.contract: Use finite, whole, nonnegative document IDs up to the largest exactly representable safe integer. Duplicate hits occupy a rank. Precision includes unfilled positions up to the cutoff. The implementation targets small per-query rankings.
api: retrieval_at_k(ranked, relevant, k)
Return precision, recall, reciprocal rank and average precision at the cutoff.
packages.logoAlt: Blyx penguin examining ranked search results through a magnifying glass.

packages.title: Backtest
packages.description: Evaluate forecasts in time order with a gap for delayed observations and disjoint test windows.
packages.contract: Choose an initial training history, a positive horizon and a nonnegative gap. A zero training window expands the history. A positive window caps its length. The final incomplete test horizon is omitted.
api: bt_fold_count(n, initial, horizon, gap), bt_fold(n, initial, horizon, gap, window, fold)
Plan training and test windows with zero-based, exclusive end indices.
bt_baselines(series, initial, horizon, gap, window)
Score a last-value and training-mean baseline on identical observations.
bt_score(series, forecasts, initial, horizon, gap)
Calculate mean absolute and signed error of submitted forecasts.
packages.logoAlt: Blyx penguin positioning training and test windows on a timeline.

packages.name: blyx-swiftlet
packages.title: Swiftlet
packages.description: Dispatch a method and request path against a table of literal and parameterized routes. Return a matched template and the methods a client can use.
packages.contract: Register a method and an absolute path template separated by one space. GET, HEAD, POST, PUT, PATCH, DELETE and OPTIONS use explicit registrations. Literal segments outrank parameters by their count. Equally specific templates use registration order. The matcher strips the query, preserves percent encoding and treats a trailing slash as significant. Hosting, URL decoding and authentication belong to the application.
api: sw_dispatch(routes, method, target)
Import router. Returns status text, matched template, and the Allow value in a three-element argument list.
sw_param(template, target, name)
Extract an encoded path parameter from a matching path. An absent capture returns an empty string.
sw_enable(mask, method), sw_status(found, mask, method)
Build a method set and apply the same status decisions as the router. Start at zero.
sw_allow(mask)
Generate the comma-separated list of registered HTTP methods.

workflow.title: Route a book catalog request
workflow.description: Pass PATCH and /books/42?preview=yes to the dispatcher. It selects /books/:id and extracts 42. Try the same method on /books/new, an explicitly read-only resource. The CGI example also serves a health check through an existing web server.
workflow.command:
git clone --depth 1 --branch v0.1.0 https://github.com/Rahulchaube1/blyx-swiftlet.git
cd blyx-swiftlet
blyxc native-run project.blyx
workflow.problem: A method error and a missing route mean different things to an HTTP client. If their responses share one fallback, clients lose the list of methods a resource accepts. RFC 9110 requires an Allow field on a 405 response.

packages.name: blyx-shrike
packages.title: Shrike
packages.description: Combine lexical and semantic search results by rank, then walk the merged list in a deterministic order.
packages.contract: Supply two ranked vectors of nonnegative integer IDs up to 2^53−1 and an offset from 0 to 1,000,000. The first occurrence in each list contributes 1/(offset + one-based position). Missing IDs contribute zero. Equal scores use ascending ID. Start the cursor at −1. Each next-result call can take quadratic time in the combined shortlist length; use this version with small candidate sets.
api: sh_valid_inputs(left, right, offset)
Validate every ID and the smoothing offset.
sh_score(left, right, id, offset)
Get the fused score of one document. Zero means absent and −1 means invalid input.
sh_next(left, right, offset, previous)
Get the next ID after a cursor, or −1 for exhaustion or invalid input. Each ID is returned once.

workflow.title: Merge two help-center searches
workflow.description: A literal-word search and a paraphrase search return different article IDs. The example prints the first three fused results. Article 21 wins because both rankers put it near the top.
workflow.command:
git clone --depth 1 --branch v0.1.0 https://github.com/Rahulchaube1/blyx-shrike.git
cd blyx-shrike
blyxc native-run project.blyx
workflow.problem: A keyword ranker and an embedding ranker return scores on different scales. Reciprocal rank fusion combines each document’s position in the lists. It gives a developer an inspectable baseline before tuning a score calibration or training a reranker.

reference.title: Cormack, Clarke and Buettcher, Reciprocal Rank Fusion

packages.name: blyx-bunting
packages.title: Bunting
packages.description: Publish a distribution as a standalone HTML table with interval labels, counts and meters. Reuse the same bin definitions in reports and tests.
packages.contract: Supply finite strictly increasing boundaries. A value exactly on a boundary belongs to the bucket above it. Bucket −1 counts missing or non-finite values. An empty boundary vector represents all finite values. The table generator validates boundaries before writing any markup. The caller supplies the HTML document around the table.
api: bu_valid(edges), bu_bucket(edges, value)
Check boundaries and locate the value by binary search.
bu_count(data, edges, bucket)
Count observations in one bucket. An invalid request returns −1.
bu_table(data, edges)
Write a captioned HTML table with explicit counts and meter values. Returns false for invalid boundaries.

workflow.title: Publish a support-queue report
workflow.description: Group eight first-reply waits at 5, 10 and 20 minutes. The resulting HTML page opens offline and exposes intervals, counts and shares as a table. Every observation contributes to one row.
workflow.command:
git clone --depth 1 --branch v0.1.0 https://github.com/Rahulchaube1/blyx-bunting.git
cd blyx-bunting
blyxc native-run project.blyx
workflow.problem: A colored chart alone can hide values from people navigating with assistive technology. W3C’s table guidance pairs data cells with headers. Bunting emits row and column headers and prints the count alongside every meter.

reference.title: W3C WAI, Tables with One Header

packages.name: blyx-wren
packages.title: Wren
packages.description: Run named checks and skips, compare floating-point measurements, and report a TAP 13 stream and a process exit status for CI.
packages.contract: Start with wr_begin, pass the returned suite to each check or skip, then call process_exit(wr_end(suite)). The producer emits a trailing TAP plan. Names are truncated at a line break or # to keep the stream unambiguous. Relative tolerance ranges from zero to one. Inputs for measurements and tolerances must be finite.
api: wr_begin(), wr_check(suite, passed, label)
Import tap. Start a TAP stream and record numbered checks.
wr_skip(suite, label, detail), wr_end(suite)
Declare a skip and finish with a plan. wr_end returns 1 when a check failed.
wr_near(actual, expected, absolute, relative)
Compare using the larger of an absolute tolerance and a tolerance scaled by the larger input magnitude.
wr_start(), wr_record(suite, passed, skipped), wr_exit(suite)
Track total, failed and skipped cases without writing TAP output.

workflow.title: Test an invoice and packing calculation
workflow.description: The suite checks a decimal invoice total and a whole-box count, then records an offline printer as a skip. Change the expected box count to see the process exit with status 1.
workflow.command:
git clone --depth 1 --branch v0.1.0 https://github.com/Rahulchaube1/blyx-wren.git
cd blyx-wren
blyxc native-run project.blyx
workflow.problem: A test that only prints an error can leave a build green. TAP defines a machine-readable result for each check and a plan stating how many results to expect. Wren couples that output to the number of failures.

packages.name: blyx-weaver
packages.title: Weaver
packages.description: Lay out equal-width tiles on small or large viewports, distribute leftover pixels and map pointer coordinates back to an item.
packages.contract: Use integer logical pixels. Width, inset, gap, minimum width and row height support values up to 1,000,000. The column limit is 1–10,000, and a grid can address 1,000,000 items. Invalid geometry produces an empty rectangle or a missed hit. Right and bottom edges are exclusive. A narrow positive content area uses one column.
api: we_columns(width, inset, gap, minimum, limit)
Choose a responsive column count; zero indicates an empty or invalid content area.
we_rect(width, inset, gap, columns, rowHeight, index)
Return [x, y, width, height] in logical pixels.
we_hit(width, inset, gap, columns, rowHeight, count, x, y)
Find the item under a pointer. Gutters, empty cells and outside positions return −1.

workflow.title: Render a file chooser as SVG
workflow.description: The example draws five file tiles in three columns. The final row has two items. Use the same geometry for touch or mouse hit testing when embedding the layout in a UI host.
workflow.browserTitle: Lay out and hit-test five tiles
workflow.command:
git clone --depth 1 --branch v0.1.0 https://github.com/Rahulchaube1/blyx-weaver.git
cd blyx-weaver
blyxc native-run project.blyx
workflow.problem: A grid can draw a tile in one place and dispatch a click to its neighbor if painting and input code round dimensions differently. CSS Grid describes how tracks and gaps form a layout. Weaver uses one integer track calculation for both drawing and input.

reference.title: W3C, CSS Grid Layout Module Level 1

packages.name: blyx-dipper
packages.title: Dipper
packages.description: Parse quoted CSV records, preserve embedded line breaks, and validate a row width before consuming a file.
packages.contract: Parse a UTF-8 string in memory. Delimiters are commas. Records accept CRLF, LF or CR; embedded quoted newlines preserve their original bytes. Spaces are data. A malformed quote discards partial results. Empty input contains zero rows; a blank line holds one empty cell. di_bad_row applies a caller-supplied column count.
api: di_parse(input), di_ok(records)
Import csv. Parse into F-prefixed field events and R end-of-row events. A lone E-prefixed event describes a syntax error.
di_cell(records, row, column)
Return one string for a present cell, including an empty cell; an absent cell returns an empty list.
di_bad_row(records, width)
Return the first zero-based row of the wrong width, −1 for success or −2 for a parse or argument error.
di_transition(state, token), di_shape(tokens)
Walk the portable quote state machine. A valid stream yields [rows, fields].

workflow.title: Import a two-column notes file
workflow.description: The importer preserves a literal quote in the first note and an embedded newline in the second. Give it a UTF-8 CSV file to check its width before reading the note column.
workflow.browserTitle: Trace the CSV parser through quoted fields
workflow.command:
git clone --depth 1 --branch v0.1.0 https://github.com/Rahulchaube1/blyx-dipper.git
cd blyx-dipper
blyxc native-run project.blyx
workflow.problem: Splitting each line on commas changes both field contents and record counts when a field contains a quoted comma or newline. RFC 4180 describes the quoting and doubled-quote rules that the Dipper parser uses.

reference.title: RFC 4180, Common Format and MIME Type for CSV Files

packages.name: blyx-kestrel
packages.title: Kestrel
packages.description: Run a bounded number of simulation ticks per rendered frame, carry fractional frame time and interpolate a moving object between updates.
packages.contract: Use whole milliseconds from 0 to 1,000,000,000, a positive step and a remainder smaller than that step. max_steps is 1–1,000,000. The clock returns an empty vector for invalid input. A frame cap discards whole ticks only. The simulation takes frame durations from the caller so a replay needs no wall clock.
api: ke_clock(carry, elapsed, step, max_steps)
Return [updates, remainder_ms, discarded_ms, interpolation_fraction]. Feed remainder_ms into the next frame.
ke_lerp(previous, current, fraction)
Interpolate a render position between the last two simulated positions.
ke_bounce(position, velocity, dt, low, high)
Advance one object on a bounded 1D track. The result holds position and velocity, including repeated wall crossings.

workflow.title: Replay a bouncing ball across a stalled frame
workflow.description: Feed the same five frame times into a fixed-step ball simulation. One 100 ms stall exceeds the catch-up limit. The replay reports positions and the number of milliseconds discarded.
workflow.command:
git clone --depth 1 --branch v0.1.0 https://github.com/Rahulchaube1/blyx-kestrel.git
cd blyx-kestrel
blyxc native-run project.blyx
workflow.problem: Rendering at a changing frame rate can change simulation speed. A long pause can also produce a burst of catch-up work. Godot’s physics interpolation guide explains the separate clocks. Kestrel makes the carry, interpolation fraction and discarded time visible to the application.

reference.title: Godot Engine, Introduction to physics interpolation

packages.name: blyx-heron
packages.title: Heron
packages.description: Track one sensor feed’s accepted messages, duplicate sequence numbers, out-of-order arrivals and missed deadlines.
packages.contract: Maintain one state per sensor. Use a monotonically increasing integer sequence and a monotonic local receipt clock in milliseconds, both at most 2^53−1. Reset the state when the sensor restarts or its sequence wraps. The gap counter records skipped IDs at acceptance time. Late arrivals do not reduce it. This release monitors application data and exposes its state to the host.
api: he_start(), he_observe(state, sequence, receipt_ms)
Initialize or update [last sequence, last receipt, accepted, duplicates, out of order, skipped IDs].
he_age(state, now)
Return milliseconds since the latest accepted observation, or −1 when unavailable.
he_status(state, now, deadline)
Return unseen, current, late or invalid. A reading remains current exactly at its deadline.

workflow.title: Audit a sensor heartbeat trace
workflow.description: Replay sequence and local receipt-time pairs. The bundled trace contains a duplicate, a two-ID gap and one out-of-order delivery. You can feed your own two-column headerless trace into the same program.
workflow.browserTitle: Detect an expired feed after a duplicate
workflow.command:
git clone --depth 1 --branch v0.1.0 https://github.com/Rahulchaube1/blyx-heron.git
cd blyx-heron
blyxc native-run project.blyx
workflow.problem: A replayed packet can make an idle sensor appear healthy if every arrival resets its last-seen timer. ROS 2 distinguishes delivery and deadline policies. Heron lets an application choose a freshness deadline and updates that timer only when it accepts a new sample.
